next.reason: Amendment 2 (§1993:p.B-17, 'general rule 10b, change to read' and 'general rule 10c, change the first sentence to read') added to 10b the continuation after imperative-statement-1 (to the end of the READ statement, NOT AT END ignored) and reworded 10c without STANDARD and for the file connector; it left the obligation. The amended §1985:VIII.4.5.4 GR10 c still reads 'If the AT END phrase is not specified, a USE AFTER EXCEPTION procedure must be associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1, and that procedure is executed' (§1985:VIII.4.5.3 SR5 refuses a READ with neither). §2023:14.9.30.4 GR24 keeps the order (status, AT END first, 'Any other applicable exception processing statements are not executed', READ unsuccessful) but its d) reads 'any applicable at end exception processing statements are executed. If there are no applicable at end exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the READ statement': the words that differ are 'must be associated' against 'If there are no applicable', so 2023 accepts and defines a READ with neither AT END nor a USE procedure, which 1985 refuses. GR24 a) also adds 'if enabled, the EC-I-O-AT-END exception condition is set to exist'. The three at end cases are carried: §2023:14.9.30.4 GR21 (optional file not present or no next record; for a relative file the key too small, 'the I-O status value associated with file-name-1 is set to '14', the at end condition exists'), with the values in §2023:9.1.13.4 GR1 and §2023:9.1.13.4 GR2 (1985: 'A value, derived from the setting of the file position indicator'). §2023:9.1.12 GR2 names the USE declarative as the applicable exception processing statements, §2023:14.9.49.4 GR6 runs it 'unless an AT END or INVALID KEY phrase takes precedence', and §2023:14.9.49.4 GR7 returns as 1985 does ('control is returned to an implicit CONTINUE statement following the input-output statement whose execution caused the exception').
